0	Map one greenhouse gas inventory to the boundary, category and assurance requirements of several disclosure regimes, documenting each reconciliation.
1	Plan an investigation of an emerging contaminant, specifying media, sampling locations, analytical methods and their reporting limits.
2	Run an incident-response drill that switches a plant or monitoring network to manual operation, recording the time to a safe state and the gaps found.
3	Identify likely sources and transport pathways of an emerging contaminant across water, soil, air and waste from site history and sampling data.
4	Review remote access to control and monitoring systems under the change procedure, removing access that is no longer needed.
5	Issue a verification opinion stating its basis, scope, materiality and unresolved issues so that users can judge the assurance given.
6	Evaluate identified misstatements against the materiality threshold, deciding whether the assertion can receive a positive verification opinion.
7	Conduct a verification site visit to a facility or project area, confirming that reported sources, equipment and land conditions exist as described.
8	Interpret emerging-contaminant results against current and proposed criteria, stating how the conclusions change if the criteria change.
9	Develop a verification plan for a greenhouse gas assertion, setting materiality, risk-based sampling and site-visit scope before evidence is gathered.
10	Sample the source data and calculations behind a greenhouse gas assertion, recalculating selected figures and recording each discrepancy found.
11	Communicate emerging-contaminant findings to affected residents while criteria are changing, explaining what is known, unknown and being done.
12	Assess cyber risk to a facility's operational technology, ranking fixes by their consequence for treatment, monitoring or safety.
13	Report anomalous control or sensor behaviour that may indicate a cyber incident, following the facility's incident procedure while keeping operation safe.
14	Compile a greenhouse gas inventory for an organization or jurisdiction, documenting boundaries, activity data, emission factors and methods for each source.
15	Recommend interim response and treatment options for an emerging contaminant, comparing performance evidence, cost and handling of residuals.
16	Quantify the uncertainty of a greenhouse gas inventory by source, identifying the sources that dominate total uncertainty.
17	Estimate value-chain emissions by category, choosing among supplier-specific, average-data and spend-based methods and stating each category's data quality.
18	Set the organizational and operational boundaries of a greenhouse gas inventory, documenting the consolidation approach and any excluded sources.
19	Maintain the evidence trail and controls behind inventory figures so that an assurance provider can trace each figure to its source data.
20	Maintain an inventory of connected control and monitoring assets with their network zone, remote-access paths and owner.
21	Check verifier independence before an engagement, declining or disclosing any relationship that would impair it.
